title: Conditional COUNT with CASE Expression
description: For each customer, count their support tickets by priority level (**high**, **medium**, **low**) in a single pivoted query using `CASE` expressions inside `COUNT()`. Show all four columns: high_count, medium_count, low_count, total_count.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE support_tickets (ticket_id INT, customer_id INT, priority VARCHAR(10), status VARCHAR(20), created_at DATE); INSERT INTO support_tickets VALUES (1,1,'high','open','2026-01-05'),(2,1,'high','closed','2026-01-10'),(3,1,'medium','open','2026-01-15'),(4,2,'low','closed','2026-01-08'),(5,2,'medium','open','2026-01-12'),(6,2,'medium','closed','2026-01-20'),(7,3,'high','open','2026-01-18'),(8,3,'low','open','2026-01-22'),(9,3,'low','closed','2026-01-25'),(10,4,'medium','closed','2026-01-28'),(11,4,'high','open','2026-02-01'),(12,4,'low','open','2026-02-05');
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(CASE WHEN priority = 'high' THEN 1 END) AS high_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN priority = 'medium' THEN 1 END) AS medium_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN priority = 'low' THEN 1 END) AS low_count, COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM support_tickets GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: 4 customers with priority counts. C1: high=2,med=1,low=0. C2: high=0,med=2,low=1. C3: high=1,med=0,low=2. C4: high=1,med=1,low=1.

hints: Wrap a CASE expression inside COUNT(): COUNT(CASE WHEN priority='high' THEN 1 END) counts only rows where the CASE returns a non-NULL value.
When CASE has no ELSE clause, non-matching rows return NULL — and COUNT() automatically skips NULLs, making this an effective conditional count.
explanation: COUNT(CASE WHEN priority='high' THEN 1 END) returns 1 for high-priority tickets and NULL otherwise; COUNT ignores NULLs, so only matching rows are counted. Repeating this pattern for each priority produces a pivot table without any JOIN or subquery. This technique works in all SQL dialects that support CASE, making it more portable than the FILTER clause approach.
